task:
BUILD SLICE S4 OF THE V3 COLONY PLANNER: THE /plan PAGE (apps/web only). BROWSER-KEPT PLANS, COMMANDER-ENTERED SLOT COUNTS, LIVE EVALUATION FROM THE API, JSON EXPORT/IMPORT. NO BACKEND, NO MIGRATIONS, NO CHANGES OUTSIDE apps/web EXCEPT TESTS THAT ALREADY LIVE IN tests/ AND ASSERT THE JOURNEY ROUTES.

Authority: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-v3-colony-planner-design.md sections 2, 2.1, 5.4, 6 and 7 (S4 row). This text wins where it is more specific; in particular the page layout below replaces the three panes listed in 5.4 (the owner reviewed a clickable mock-up on 2026-10-31 and chose this layout). Follow CLAUDE.md "Web / Frontend" and docs/development/v3-application-stack-decision.md (Svelte 5 runes, SvelteKit 2, TypeScript, pnpm 11; Babylon is not involved).

Do NOT touch: apps/api/, sql/, packages/, apps/web/src/lib/api/generated (regenerating it is not needed: getV3PlanCatalogue, evaluateV3Plan and listV3PlanBodies, including the S3a.1 `belts` field, already exist in the generated client), the legacy frontend/ tree. No new dependencies.

DATA AND STATE
1. API (use only the generated facade under apps/web/src/lib/api/, the way other features do):
   - catalogue: getV3PlanCatalogue (load once);
   - bodies: listV3PlanBodies for the `system` query parameter (id64 string);
   - evaluation: evaluateV3Plan with PlanRequestV1 built from the current plan, re-run after every change (debounce about 250 ms; ignore stale responses). 400 responses carry PlanInvalidV1: show the message in the summary pane, keep the last good evaluation greyed. Never compute CP numbers in the browser: every cost, total, result, reason, port number and payer suggestion shown comes from the evaluate response.
2. Plan storage: reuse the existing `colonyProjects` store (apps/web/src/lib/persistence/stores.ts, record type ColonyProjectRecord in storage.ts). No new storage key.
   - One ColonyProjectRecord per system_id64 for the planner (create it on first edit; follow the store's existing id conventions).
   - Sites are `build_plan_placements` entries with `schema: "cpe_site_v1"` and fields `site_id` (stable, e.g. crypto.randomUUID()), `facility_id`, `body_ref` (the body's `body_id` string or null), `slot_kind` ("orbital"|"surface"), `status` ("planned"|"building"|"complete"|"demolished"), `name` (≤64 chars, may be empty). Array order is the build order. The first entry is the Primary Port.
   - Commander-entered slot counts live in `selected_body_assignments.cpe_slots_v1` as `{ [body_id or a belt's location reference]: { orbital_slots: number|null, surface_slots: number|null } }`; a site on a belt has the belt's location reference as `body_ref`; leave every other key of selected_body_assignments untouched.
   - Placements without `schema: "cpe_site_v1"` (old V2 planner) are shown read-only in a collapsed "Older plan items (read-only)" section and are never rewritten or removed.
   - Put the codec (record ⇄ planner model ⇄ PlanRequestV1) in a pure module with unit tests, including a round trip and the V2-placement preservation.
3. PlanRequestV1 mapping: system_id64; bodies = every body except belt clusters (a belt's resolved cluster is sent once, as the belt entry below), with body_ref=body_id, orbital_slots/surface_slots from cpe_slots_v1 (null when not entered), is_landable from the bodies API, is_ringed = has_rings; plus one entry per belt with body_ref = the belt's resolved location reference (see the Asteroid belts point under PAGE LAYOUT B), orbital_slots from cpe_slots_v1[that reference], surface_slots 0, is_landable false, is_ringed true (confirmed in game by the owner on 2026-10-31: the construction screen offered an Asteroid Base, 5 Tier 2 points, at "<system> A A Belt Cluster 1" — the game names a belt build after the belt's first cluster even though the system map shows only the belt; so the "+" picker on a belt offers ringed-orbital facilities such as the Asteroid Base, alongside the other orbital ones); sites = the cpe_site_v1 placements in order (respect the API limit of 300 sites: block adding more with a clear message).
4. Route: create apps/web/src/routes/plan/+page.svelte (and +page.ts only if the codebase pattern needs it); remove `plan` from apps/web/src/params/journey.ts and add/adjust the test that asserts the journey matcher. `/plan?system=<id64>` is the entry used by Inspect ("Continue to Plan"), Explore ("Plan here") and the app shell ("Open plan"); with no `system` parameter fall back to the existing `selectedSystem` store, and if there is none show a short "Pick a system in Explore or Inspect first" message with links. Keep `selectedSystem` in sync with the planned system.

PAGE LAYOUT (wide screens: three columns — System | Build order | Summary; phone width: stacked in that order, no horizontal page scroll). Feature code in apps/web/src/lib/features/plan/.
A. Header: system name, id64, crumbs Explore › Inspect › Plan, a "Now / After the plan" toggle for the points shown in the summary, buttons Export plan (JSON download of the planner's own placements + slot counts + system id64, versioned `{"schema":"cpe_plan_export_v1", ...}`) and Import plan (file input accepting that same schema, validated, replacing the planner's placements and slot counts for this system after a confirm step). If the Inspect page already loads a Finder rating/archetype for a system through the facade, show the same two facts in the header; if not, leave them out (do not add API calls).
B. System pane — a body tree, like Raven Colonial's system view but showing more at a glance:
   - Tree from `direct_parent_body_id`, connector lines between parent and children. Barycentres are not rows: attach their children to the barycentre's nearest non-barycentre ancestor (or the root).
   - Asteroid belts (owner, checked in game on 2026-10-31): the game's system map shows each asteroid belt as ONE buildable item, and that item is the belt's first cluster — the construction screen names the location "<system> A A Belt Cluster 1". The other clusters never appear in the game. The bodies response has a `belts` list (belt_id, name, parent_body_id, ring_type, reserve, mass, radii; added in S3a.1, already in the generated client) and the cluster bodies (body_type belt cluster, named "<belt name> Cluster N"). Show each belt as one buildable row under its parent body, in the parent's child order, with a belt/asteroid disc, the belt's short name (e.g. "A Belt"), ring type/reserve badges, a "+" button and an orbital slot box only (no surface box). The row's location reference (`body_ref`, slot-count key and site placement) is the body_id of that belt's cluster with the lowest N (normally "Cluster 1"), matched by the name prefix "<belt name> Cluster "; only when the data has no cluster for the belt use "belt:<belt_id>". Every other cluster body is hidden everywhere (tree, pickers, move-to-body select) and is never a site location. Put this belt/cluster resolution in one pure, unit-tested function.
   - Each body row: a disc coloured by body_type (star / planet; belts get their own asteroid style) and sized by radius_km (sensible clamps); the short body name (the full name minus the system name prefix); small feature badges with a text title and accessible name: landable, rings, geological N, biological N, volcanism (when volcanism is non-null and not "No volcanism"), terraformable (terraforming_state non-null and not "Not terraformable"), atmosphere (non-null and not "No atmosphere"); a "+" button "Add a build on <body>"; two slot boxes: orbital "used/total" and surface "used/total" (surface shows "–" and is not editable when is_landable is false; total unknown shows "?"; a box is highlighted when used exceeds total). "used" counts this body's cpe_site_v1 sites of that slot kind whose status is not demolished.
   - Clicking a slot box opens a small popover editor: −, +, "Unknown", "Done"; range 0–64; it says the value is entered by the commander and that orbital slots should be copied from Architect Mode.
   - Under each body, its sites as compact tiles that wrap: build-order number, status (word in the accessible name, glyph visually: complete ●, building ◐, planned ○, demolished ✕), facility name, tier badge (T1/T2/T3), the site name (a "Types only / Types + names" toggle hides names), and for planned sites the result as icon+word in the accessible name (OK ✓, Blocked ✕, Needs info ?). Blocked tiles are visibly tinted. Clicking a tile opens the Why panel for that step and selects it in the build order.
   - The "+" picker lists catalogue facilities grouped Orbital / Surface (Surface only when is_landable is not false; ringed-orbital facilities only when has_rings is true), each with tier, CP cost/gain and prerequisites; choosing one appends a planned site on that body.
   - Sites whose body_ref is null are listed in an "Unplaced" group at the bottom.
C. Build order pane: filter chips All / Blocked / Needs info / On <selected body>; an ordered list of every site: index, name, "Primary Port" label on the first, facility · slot kind · body, status, cost and gain chips, "port #n" for escalating ports, running Tier 2 / Tier 3 after the step, result chip (icon + word), "Move up" / "Move down" buttons (moves are allowed only among planned sites, never above the Primary Port), a "Why?" button, and an expandable edit row: rename, status select, move to another body (body select filtered by slot kind/landable), remove. Once the Primary Port is complete it cannot be moved, removed or changed to another facility (RB-0008); say so where the controls would be.
D. Summary pane: Tier 2 and Tier 3 for the selected view (Now / After the plan) — negative values visibly marked; next Tier 2 and next Tier 3 port cost; counts of OK / Blocked / Needs info; "Needs attention": the first blocked step (button jumps to it), the plan-level check when more than five sites are building (RB-0007), and the number of bodies that have sites but unknown slot counts (button selects the first); "Building now" list (each opens Why).
E. Why panel: a drawer from the right (dialog semantics, focus moves into it, Escape and a Close button close it and return focus): step number and name, result, every reason in plain words, a small Before / Cost / After / Earns table with the port number, the payer suggestions from the API with an "Add before this step" button (inserts a planned site of that facility on a body with a free slot of the right kind, or unplaced if none), and the rule explanations (rule id, status, title, statement, quote and page) returned by the API.

ACCESSIBILITY (design section 6): everything works from the keyboard; reordering uses the Move buttons; the number of blocked steps is announced in a polite live region after each evaluation; colour is never the only signal; respect reduced motion; dark mode works through the app's existing tokens.

TESTS
- Vitest unit tests: codec round trip and V2 preservation; tree building (barycentre children re-parented, belts buildable under their parent, each belt resolved to its lowest-numbered cluster or to belt:<id>, other clusters hidden and never offered as locations); slot "used" counting; plan actions (add, insert-before, move up/down rules, remove, status change, Primary Port protection, 300-site limit); PlanRequestV1 mapping; export/import validation (schema, size cap 2 MB, rejects other systems unless confirmed).
- Component tests for the drawer focus/escape behaviour and the slot editor, following existing apps/web test patterns.
- Cypress main path (design section 6), following how existing apps/web Cypress specs provide API data: open from Inspect → add a port and two installations → see the budget and a Blocked step → fix the order → reload, the plan is still there.
- The journey matcher test for removing `plan`.

VALIDATION: in apps/web: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`; run the new Cypress spec headless if the runner allows, otherwise say so. From the repo root run the Python tests that mention the journey routes or apps/web/src/params (search tests/ for "journey") with CPython 3.14 and report counts.

SUMMARY: list changed files with one-line purposes; describe the storage shape actually written; list any design point you could not meet and why.
